official_measurement_examples.fact: Outline planning permission can establish the principle and parameters of development while reserving specified details for later approval.
Reserved matters are appearance, access, landscaping, layout and scale, subject to what was actually reserved by the outline permission.
Use and amount of development must be sufficiently described at outline stage; outline permission is not a blank permission for any later scheme.
Article 5(3) requires outline applications to indicate areas for access points even where access is reserved.
Details submitted as formal parts of an outline application cannot silently be treated as illustrative if the applicant has not identified them as such.
Current Southwark guidance updated 7 July 2026 states reserved-matters applications are normally submitted within three years of outline permission, subject to the actual condition.
Approval of reserved matters does not replace separate building regulations, environmental permits or other statutory consents.
Outline or reserved-matters approval does not establish ownership, access rights, infrastructure capacity or final development yield.

core_rules: outline permission is not approval of all details
reserved matters must match what was reserved
use and amount remain constrained by outline permission
illustrative material is not automatically approved detail
reserved-matters deadline must use actual permission condition
approval of reserved matters is not new ownership evidence
outline permission does not prove commencement
reserved matters do not replace other statutory consents
outline permission does not establish infrastructure capacity
reserved matters approval does not prove build-out
permission boundary is not cadastral title boundary
appeal outcome must retain decision date
no parcel outline clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
site-specific conditions control over generic assumptions
